body:
WHAT
There are two permission stances: normal, where every tool class is allowed by default and only target-shaped guards ask (deletions, edits to .magentra/.env, edits outside the workspace), and OVERDRIVE, where nothing asks at all. A call is resolved in a fixed order: deny rules first, then the protected-path guard, then the deletion guard, then allow rules (settings, session, exact grants), then the stance default. Deny rules refuse even in OVERDRIVE.

WHY
Without a fixed resolution order a broad allow rule could bypass the deletion guard, or OVERDRIVE could silently ignore the user's own deny configuration.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/permissions.ts — PermissionEngine.check() (the ordered branches), PermissionEngine.overdrive / setOverdrive(), stanceDefault() (always 'allow'), matches(), matchesExplicit(), parseRule(), globToRegex(), addSessionAllow()/removeSessionAllow(). engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.setOverdrive() (calls permissions.setOverdrive and adds the OVERDRIVE_PROMPT_SECTION).

TEST CHECKLIST
1. A deny rule 'Bash(rm *)' beats everything: check() for subject 'rm -rf x' returns allowed:false, source:'rule' without calling requestApproval, even with setOverdrive(true) and an allow rule for the same subject.
2. A protected-path edit (editProtectedPath set) asks before allow rules are consulted: with a broad 'Write' allow rule, requestApproval is still called with source 'protected-path'.
3. A deletion (deletionSubject defined) asks even when 'Bash(*)' or a session allow for 'Bash' matches, but an explicit 'Bash(rm -rf ./tmp/*)' rule lets that exact subject through with source 'rule'.
4. With no guards triggered, a matching allow rule returns {allowed:true, source:'rule'} and an unmatched ordinary command returns {allowed:true, source:'mode'} (stance default is allow) without prompting.
5. setOverdrive(true) makes a deletion, a protected-path edit and an out-of-workspace edit all resolve allowed:true with no requestApproval call, while a deny rule still refuses.
